name: Sikao Guo, Ph.D.
title: Computational Biophysics & Scientific Software
description: Sikao Guo develops computational methods and open-source C++/Python software for protein conformational sampling, biomolecular self-assembly, and high-performance simulation.

experience.summary: Protein conformational sampling, all-atom assessment of samplers, and generated interfaces for structural-biology tools.
highlights: Extended inverse-kinematics sampling in the Structural Bioinformatics Library to flexible protein fragments and intrinsically disordered regions, with released-endpoint SE(3) moves, Ramachandran-informed selection, and clash checks.
Built AttnPacker/OpenMM workflows for all-atom assessment and comparative benchmarking of geometric and generative protein samplers. Manuscript in preparation.
Designed AutoCLIP, a specification-driven framework generating PyMOL, VMD, and web interfaces for structural-biology tools. First-author arXiv preprint, 2026.

experience.location: T. C. Jenkins Department of Biophysics, Baltimore, Maryland, USA
experience.summary: Structure-resolved reaction–diffusion models of clathrin and HIV lattices, and parallel simulation with NERDSS.
highlights: Developed structure-resolved reaction–diffusion models of adaptor-dependent clathrin lattice stability, predicting a critical nucleus of approximately 25 clathrin under cell-like conditions. First-author study, PLOS Computational Biology, 2022.
Modeled local remodeling of the immature HIV lattice and identified conditions permitting Gag–Pol encounters while retaining large-scale lattice structure. First-author study, eLife, 2023.

Led the C++/MPI parallelization of the particle-based reaction–diffusion simulator NERDSS using spatial domain decomposition; assessed accuracy against theory and serial simulations and scaling across up to 96 processors. First-author study, Journal of Computational Chemistry, 2025.
Co-developed ioNERDSS structure–simulation–analysis workflows. Contributed modeling and simulations to studies of dynamin nanoclusters and secretion-catalyzed protein biomaterials.

education.institution: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China
education.detail: Advisor: Ping Xie. Dissertation on theoretical and numerical models of dimeric kinesin motors.

focusText: Biomolecular self-assembly and remodeling; protein conformational sampling; stochastic reaction–diffusion and kinetic models; reproducible scientific software and high-performance computing.
bio: I am a computational biophysicist and Research Engineer in the Algorithms–Biology–Structure (ABS) team at Inria Sophia Antipolis, working with Frédéric Cazals. I extend inverse-kinematics sampling in the Structural Bioinformatics Library to flexible protein fragments and intrinsically disordered regions, and build AutoCLIP, which generates PyMOL, VMD, and web interfaces for structural-biology tools from one specification.

From 2020 to 2025 I was a postdoctoral researcher and then Assistant Research Scientist in the T. C. Jenkins Department of Biophysics at Johns Hopkins University with Margaret E. Johnson, modeling clathrin and immature HIV lattices and leading the C++/MPI parallelization of the NERDSS reaction–diffusion simulator. I received my Ph.D. in condensed matter physics from the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (advisor: Ping Xie), working on models of dimeric kinesin motors, and my B.S. in physics from Nankai University.
